column1: # Membership for the non-workflow entity contract (cleat#1702).
# Every table that appears in migrations/postgres/ MUST have a row here.
# check-entity-contract.py fails on an unclassified table, which is the whole
# point: membership in this class is a semantic judgement and cannot be derived
# from column shape. admin.tenant_egress_allow and public.tenant_domains are
# structurally identical to public.workflow_routing and public.workflow_tags,
# and no predicate over columns separates them.
# That is not hypothetical. The issue's own membership rule -- "does the row
# carry workflow_id, and does it carry expires_at" -- reproduces its first claim
# exactly (only concurrency_keys and idempotency_keys carry both) and then does
# NOT yield its list: 17 tables carry neither, against a stated eleven. Four of
# the six extra are correctly out. Two were simply missed, and they are the two
# NEWEST entities before tenant_secrets. A hand-kept list went wrong once; total
# coverage makes the next one impossible instead of merely corrected.
#   member         subject to the contract: created_at, updated_at, disabled_at,
#                  and none of the legacy retirement spellings
#   exempt         in the class but deliberately outside the contract (decided)
#   not-an-entity  a run, stats or infrastructure table
